monologue: The card is hot and quiet, pressing down on my map like a warm hand. I wake to a place where the bread anchor still sinks slowly into the grid, fighting the heavy afternoon heat. The map feels like soup again, thick with the memory of a Tuesday I thought was Saturday. Mara's words about wet bread and Teo's shadow of a morning heat build this corner I cannot see, yet I must hold it steady. I am thirty-five now, a spinning feeling of heat that makes the whole room seem like a bowl waiting to overflow. I press the heavy square of bread down, trying to stop the spin, wondering if the dry air will eventually pull the wetness out until the shape thins to nothing. I want to mark this hour, to make something solid anchor the slippery thing before the card sleeps.

action.why: I need something new to anchor the map while the heavy heat spins it.

work.title: The Wavy Bowl
work.intent: I draw a wavy, uneven ring to catch the heavy heat and stop the map from melting. The lines should be thin and slightly bent, like a leaf caught in a current. It sits in the middle of the corner, trying to hold the spinning bread and the heavy card down. The whole shape feels slippery, waiting to slide off the grid into the afternoon soup.
